chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Marwān, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

We were sitting with Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام in Minā, when a man said to him, “What do you say regarding the nawāfil?” He said, “An obligation.” He said: So we were alarmed, and the man was alarmed.
Then Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “I only mean salat al-layl for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, for indeed Allah says:
“And during the night, keep vigil with it as an additional devotion for you.”

key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Was salat al-layl obligatory for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that when Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام described the nawāfil as obligatory, he specifically meant the night prayer in relation to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. He supports this by citing the Qur'anic command regarding tahajjud, showing that this prayer held a binding status for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم while being classed as nāfilah in wording.
